# Reproduction of Eisaguirre et al. (2020, *Ecology*) from raw PISCO data

*Generated by `code/R/17_eisaguirre_reproduction.R`. All reproduced numbers are
from that script; published values are from Eisaguirre et al. 2020, Ecology
101(5):e02993. This is the paired-design Channel-Islands cascade comparator for the
Donham & Stier manuscript, complementing the unpaired Kumagai 2024 comparison
(scripts 14–16).*

---

## Why a from-raw reproduction

Eisaguirre et al. (2020) is the closest published analogue to our trophic-cascade
claim: a **paired inside/outside MPA design** in the western Northern Channel
Islands, on the **same PISCO kelp-forest monitoring program** we and Kumagai (2024)
use, showing that protected predator guilds (sheephead + lobster) buffer the
urchin→kelp cascade after the sea-star (Pycnopodia) was lost to wasting disease, with
predator **size structure** as the key mechanism. Eisaguirre archived no data or
code, so we rebuilt the analysis from the raw PISCO fish + swath tables we already
hold (`MLPA_kelpforest_fish_2024.csv`, `MLPA_kelpforest_swath_2024.csv`) and checked
our reproduced numbers against their published ones.

## What we reproduced (their design)

- **Sites:** western NCI — San Miguel (SMI), Santa Rosa (SRI), western Santa Cruz
  (SCI); no-take SMRs + paired reference reefs; 2010–2017, 2013 excluded; pre-disease
  2010–2012 vs post-disease 2014–2017.
- **Response:** ln(purple-urchin density per 60-m² benthic transect); Gaussian LMM
  (`lme4`), reef random intercept, depth a fixed covariate, no island RE.
- **Predators:** sunflower star (Pycnopodia, PYCHEL), CA sheephead (SPUL, adults
  ≥15 cm, density × mean-length interaction), protection; sea-star × protection and
  sheephead density × length interactions; lobster and red urchin excluded as they
  did. Candidate models AICc-ranked.

**Documented departures** (the paper underspecifies these): the exact 7-site list is
not named — we used all western-NCI no-take-SMR reefs with in-period data (**14
reefs / 29 survey sites**); and temperature — they used daily MUR satellite SST,
unavailable locally, so we used the **in-situ survey temperature** averaged per
reef-year.

## Result: the cascade structure reproduces; the fine-grained partial effects do not

| Quantity | Reproduced | Eisaguirre 2020 |
|---|---|---|
| Sheephead size quartiles (adults ≥15 cm) | 19 / 26 / 39 cm | 24.56 / 31.50 / 38.15 cm |
| Mean sheephead TL, MPA vs reference | 32.3 / 29.4 cm (larger inside) | MPA larger (ref 30.34) |
| **Post-disease top model (AICc)** | **sheephead(dens×len) + protection** | **sheephead(dens×len) + protection (wt 0.99)** |
| Pre-disease top model | includes sunflower star | temp+depth+seastar (wt 0.51) |
| **Protection: urchins higher outside MPA** | **YES (MPA −1.47 log, p<0.001; 614 vs 339 / 60 m²)** | **YES (urchin barrens outside MPA)** |
| Sea-star ~ urchin, bivariate (pre) | −0.22 (negative) | negative |
| Sheephead ~ urchin, bivariate (post) | −0.23 (negative) | negative |
| Macroalgae ~ purple urchin | −0.40 (negative) | negative (wt 1.00) |
| Sea-star *partial* effect (mixed model) | **+0.26 (did NOT reproduce)** | negative (top predictor) |
| Sheephead size-structured *partial* suppression | **did NOT reproduce** | large suppress at lower density |

**The robust, reproducible core.** Every structural and design-level result
reproduces: MPAs hold significantly fewer urchins (the protection effect, the
backbone of their argument); sheephead are larger inside reserves; the post-disease
model selection lands on *exactly* their top model (sheephead density × length +
protection); and the bivariate cascade signs — sea-star↓urchin, sheephead↓urchin,
urchin↓kelp — all match. The sheephead size quartiles and mean lengths land within a
few cm of theirs.

**What did not reproduce — and why it's informative.** The two *partial* coefficients
that carry their headline mechanism flip or vanish in our re-derivation:

1. The **sunflower-star partial effect** is negative bivariately (−0.22, matching)
   but turns **positive** once a reef random intercept and the other covariates are
   included — the sea-star↓urchin signal is largely a *between-reef* gradient (cold,
   productive western reefs have more stars and fewer urchins) that a reef intercept
   absorbs.
2. The **size-structured sheephead suppression** does not survive once `protection`
   is in the model: sheephead abundance and protection are collinear (MPAs have more,
   larger sheephead), so the partial sheephead coefficients turn positive — the exact
   collinearity Eisaguirre themselves flagged when they *excluded* lobster (r = 0.78
   with sheephead). With our larger reef set the same collinearity now bites
   sheephead. We therefore could not reproduce the "11 large vs 91 small sheephead to
   hold urchins at 2/m²" calculation; we present the **bivariate** relationship
   (Fig 4) instead of a partial-model prediction.

This is the same lesson as the Kumagai methods comparison (scripts 14–16): the
**robust, design-level conclusions (protection buffers the cascade; kelp/urchin and
predator/urchin signs) are insensitive to analytical choices, whereas the
fine-grained partial coefficients are highly sensitive** to the site set, covariate
collinearity, and random-effect structure — none of which the paper fully specifies.
Two independent paired-design analyses (ours and Eisaguirre's) converge on the
*structure* of MPA-buffered resilience while disagreeing on the *partial mechanism
attribution*, which is exactly where observational cascade inference is weakest.

## Reproducibility

`code/R/17_eisaguirre_reproduction.R` reads optional raw PISCO files from
`DONHAM_DATA_REPO_PISCO` or the default local data-repo path; it is
**standalone** (not in `run_all.R`) and skips gracefully if that raw data is
absent. Outputs:
`tables/table_s_eisaguirre_reproduction.csv` (reproduced vs published),
`tables/table_s_eisaguirre_models.csv` (AICc model selection, pre/post),
`plots/fig_s_eisaguirre_fig3_urchin_seastar.{pdf,png}` (pre-disease urchin~sea-star),
`plots/fig_s_eisaguirre_fig4_urchin_sheephead.{pdf,png}` (post-disease urchin~sheephead
by protection).

### Figure legends

**Figure S — Reproduced Eisaguirre Fig 3 (pre-disease, 2010–2012).** Purple-urchin
density vs sunflower-sea-star density per 60-m² benthic transect at western-NCI
reefs, inside MPAs (blue) and reference sites (orange), with linear fits ± 95% CI.
The negative bivariate association (more sea stars → fewer urchins) reproduces.

**Figure S — Reproduced Eisaguirre Fig 4 (post-disease, 2014–2017).** Purple-urchin
density vs CA-sheephead density (adults ≥15 cm) by protection. Urchins decline with
sheephead density and are lower inside MPAs — the reproducible bivariate suppression.
(We show the empirical relationship rather than a partial-model prediction because
the sheephead–protection collinearity prevents reproduction of the partial
size-structured effect; see text.)
